title: Bridgekeeper: Dependency Claim-and-Release Protocol for Roadmap Sequencing
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: cross-team roadmap handoffs currently rely on ad-hoc signals (Slack threads, meetings, spreadsheets). This causes duplicate work, missed sequencing (especially between Dedicated and Private releases), and opaque ownership during cutovers.

Proposal: implement 'Bridgekeeper' — a lightweight claim-and-release protocol + small orchestration surface for roadmap dependencies. Bridgekeeper lets a team "claim" a dependency (take ownership for sequencing and validation) and then "release" it when the dependency is verified or rolled back. The protocol will be surfaced as: (1) policy docs and checklist, (2) a minimal RoadmapOps UI to claim/release and show status, (3) an event-driven webhook for eng/design/security infra to subscribe to state changes, and (4) an escalation path for stuck claims (PagerDuty + SLACK escalation bot).

Scope: MVP covers cross-team dependencies for initiatives that touch runtime, console, and private deployments. Focus first on Interlock flows that block canaries and cutovers: model pinning, KV cache changes, RBAC migrations, and major console UX flows.

Trade-offs considered:
- Lightweight UI vs full dependency engine: MVP will be a thin UI and API rather than a complex rules engine to get rapid adoption.
- Protocol strictness vs speed: allow 'soft claims' (informational) and 'hard claims' (blocking for cutover) to avoid blocking low-risk work.
- Centralized vs distributed ownership: we default to owner-team claim but support secondary stakeholders for verification steps.

Deliverables:
- Public Bridgekeeper PRD (Confluence) documenting claim lifecycle and SLAs.
- RoadmapOps UI wireframe and a small backend endpoint (/api/v1/claims).
- Escalation playbook wired to PagerDuty and a Slack channel bot.
- Integration guides for ENG/DES/SEC/INFRA to subscribe to webhooks.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- 60% of cross-team cutovers use Bridgekeeper claims for sequencing.
- Mean time to resolve a blocked claim drops by 35%.
- Number of last-minute cutover rollbacks due to missed dependencies reduced by 50%.
acceptance_criteria: Claim lifecycle documented in Confluence with examples (soft/hard claim)
Minimal RoadmapOps UI enables claim, add reviewers, set claim type, and release
Webhook schema published and two teams (ENG + DESIGN) have integrated consumers
Escalation workflow triggers PagerDuty after configurable SLA and notifies #bridgekeeper channel
Demo cutover run using Bridgekeeper claim for a non-production Dedicated canary
